ux.title: Responsive conference schedule and event navigation
ux.intro: TCT 2014 combined conference content with a responsive Week-at-a-Glance schedule, day filtering and expandable session information.

panels.title: Week-at-a-Glance schedule
panels.copy: The schedule organized conference sessions by day and used interactive filtering so visitors could narrow the visible program without leaving the page.

panels.title: Desktop and mobile behavior
panels.copy: Separate desktop and mobile schedule treatments used Bootstrap collapse behavior and responsive layouts to keep dense program information usable across screen sizes.

panels.title: Conference presentation
panels.copy: The site combined event branding, slider content, navigation and schedule interactions within the CRF Joomla conference template.

ux.title: Interactive conference navigation and Week-at-a-Glance schedule
ux.intro: TCT 2015 paired a video-led conference homepage with custom vector navigation and a responsive Week-at-a-Glance schedule.

panels.title: Custom vector navigation
panels.copy: A custom triangular JavaScript/SVG navigation interface linked directly to major conference destinations including the agenda, organizers, satellite programs, exhibits and CME.

panels.title: Responsive Week-at-a-Glance
panels.copy: The conference schedule used day filters, expandable session rows and separate desktop/mobile accordion behavior implemented with JavaScript/jQuery and Bootstrap collapse.

panels.title: Video-led homepage
panels.copy: The homepage layered the vector navigation over an HTML5 video treatment and integrated conference content, carousel sections and event calls to action.

ux.title: Conference disclosure navigator
ux.intro: The Dallas Leipzig interface uses a stacked section navigator with a selected state and an adjacent content panel so disclosure information can change within the page without sending the visitor to a separate screen.

panels.title: Active section state
panels.copy: A vertical stack of section labels provides a clear current selection. The active row changes treatment and uses a directional arrow to connect the selected label to the content panel.

panels.title: Expandable / changing content
panels.copy: The component supports changing or expanded conference content within the same interface rather than requiring a separate page for every disclosure section.

panels.title: Visual relationship
panels.copy: The selected navigation state and adjacent content panel work together as one component, keeping the active topic visually connected to the information being displayed.

workflow.title: Handle selection states
workflow.copy: Manage active, collapsed and expanded states so the selected section remains visually connected to its content.

workflow.label: 03 · MOTION
workflow.title: Animate state changes
workflow.copy: Use front-end animation and JavaScript behavior to make content changes and disclosure transitions feel deliberate rather than abrupt.

workflow.label: 04 · RESPONSIVE

workflow.copy: Fit the component into the responsive Dallas Leipzig conference interface and surrounding page structure.

ux.title: One event identity across many user touchpoints
ux.intro: The design problem was larger than a single invitation. Guests encountered event information through invitation components, response materials, hotel and directions information, email and supporting event pieces.

panels.title: Information hierarchy
panels.copy: The invitation, RSVP, dinner selection, hotel information and directions each carried different information while remaining visibly part of the same event package.

panels.title: System consistency
panels.copy: The Gatsby-inspired identity was extended across print, email, website graphics, sponsorship and event materials instead of redesigning every touchpoint independently.
